title: Robustness of Quantum Signal Processing and Resource-aware Polynomial Design
authors: Thiago O. Maciel, Giancarlo Camilo, Allan Tosta, Daniel Stilck-França, Leandro Aolita, Thais de Lima Silva
abstract: Quantum signal processing (QSP) realizes operator functions through polynomial transformations of a finite degree. In addition to function approximation errors, realistic implementations incur algorithmic errors also when encoding the input operator and in synthesizing gates into a discrete fault-tolerant gate set. We provide an end-to-end analysis of these errors and show that the input error propagation is governed by the operator-Lipschitz constant $L_\star$ of the implemented function. We then derive an efficient classical algorithm to compute tight lower and upper bounds on $L_\star$, and we show that these bounds induce in turn lower and upper bounds on the total quantum-resource cost (for instance, $T$-gate count) needed for QSP implementations compatible with a target total error. We further devise a procedure to search for a polynomial with minimum cost based solely on its coefficients, yielding a resource-aware polynomial-design procedure for QSP. We illustrate the resulting method for ground state energy estimation via eigenvalue thresholding for the H$_6$ molecular Hamiltonian. In the tested hardware profiles, the resource-aware family improves the total-error budget and reduces the modeled $T$-gate count by $51.9\%$--$56.7\%$ relative to the standard analytical polynomial obtained from an error-function approximation.
summary: This work develops a resource-aware methodology for Quantum Signal Processing (QSP) by quantifying the impact of multiple error sources, notably through the operator-Lipschitz constant $L_\star$. By optimizing polynomial coefficients based on a total error budget, the authors demonstrate a significant reduction in required quantum resources, such as T-gates, for tasks like molecular energy estimation.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the robustness of Quantum Signal Processing (QSP) and Quantum Singular-Value Transformation (QSVT) algorithms against multiple sources of algorithmic errors.
main_result: A resource-aware polynomial design procedure was developed that significantly reduces the modeled T-gate count (by 51.9%–56.7%) compared to standard analytical methods for ground state energy estimation.
method: It establishes an end-to-end error budget incorporating function approximation, input operator error (governed by the operator-Lipschitz constant $L_\star$), and gate synthesis errors, optimizing polynomial coefficients to minimize total resource cost.
model_or_system: The analysis is applied to implementing functions of operators, such as for ground state energy estimation using the $H_6$ molecular Hamiltonian, within the framework of the Linear Combination of Unitaries (LCU) model.
key_observables: Operator-Lipschitz constant ($L_\star$), total quantum-resource cost (T-gate count), and the three error components ($\varepsilon_{	ext{app}}, \varepsilon_{	ext{input}}, \varepsilon_{	ext{synth}}$).
important_parameters: Target total error budget, polynomial degree ($N$), and the specific Hamiltonian ($H_6$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the implemented function is operator-Lipschitz and relies on developing efficient classical algorithms to bound $L_\star$ and the resource cost.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes detail the derivation of error bounds and the comparison of resource costs.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the error sources and the role of $L_\star$, then developing algorithms to bound $L_\star$, and finally proposing a resource-aware polynomial design procedure that minimizes the total error budget for practical quantum simulations.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous, resource-aware framework for designing quantum algorithms, directly addressing the practical limitations imposed by hardware noise and finite resources in quantum simulation.
